newsitem.title: FINLAND: Invesco manager sees value in Raisio.
newsitem.headline: Invesco manager sees value in Raisio.

text.p: Invesco Asset Management, part of British fund manager Invesco Plc, still sees value in Finnish food and chemicals group Raision Tehtaat shares, portfolio manager Steven Chamberlain said on Thursday.

"It looks expensive on present-year earnings and the year after...but if one just takes future projections and discount back, then I think the stock is of good value," Chamberlain told Reuters at an investment seminar.
Raisio has risen very sharply this year, mostly on high expectations for its Benecol margarine which will not reach international markets this year, maybe not even next.
Raisio is one of the Finnish securities held by unit trusts managed by Invesco.

The unit trusts also own shares in small companies including data services group TT-Tieto, office furniture maker Martela, industrial cranes maker KCI-Konecranes and prefabricated sauna maker Saunatec .
Their most recent investment in a Finnish company was in compass maker Suunto, he said.
Invesco's biggest holding in Finland is in TT-Tieto, Chamberlain said, but declined to say how big the stake was.
Asked where in Finland Invesco would turn next, he said he might consider buying cyclical shares.
"I think we are probably getting closer to the point of investing in some cyclicals," he said, but declined to elaborate.
Chamberlain said Invesco was not planning to buy shares in telecoms group Nokia, where it used to have a stake.
"The problem that we would have is we still don't find a lot of visibility about future earnings in Nokia and that leaves us a little wary," Chamberlain said.
Invesco's unit trusts' current holdings in Finnish companies are worth $30-$40 million, he said.
